reference: Independent system Git CLI (`git`, required per parity case) running from the reference Bash PATH. The reference side validates each expected status and is compared byte-for-byte on stdout; cases with deterministic repository metadata also compare the full fixture tree. Git configuration is isolated from host configuration, and a relative private template contains only the matching default description and exclude files, avoiding installed sample hooks.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata contract; this checks loadable discovery only and is not operation coverage.

Nested init and repository discovery, config round trips, binary loose-object hash/read and refs, index staging/status/diff, deterministic commits and history, fixture-local git mv/rm/clean, local clone, and a missing-object error.

Complete tree comparison for init, config, and the error case. Index/object/history/local-clone cases compare Git's observable output and statuses while documenting variable index stat data, reflog timestamps, compression streams, or local-clone storage strategy.
Missing-object status and exact diagnostics across cat-file modes
exclusions: Remote clone/fetch/push require a disposable in-namespace protocol mock and are deferred; no real network target is used.
Signing and interactive editor behavior require a fake signing helper and bounded PTY fixture and are deferred.
This focused suite does not establish full Git command or option compatibility.

cases.purpose: Check Bash reports git as a builtin and exposes the documented one-line help description; metadata only, not Git operation coverage.
cases.stdout:
builtin
git - Run a git command, in a forked child.

cases.purpose: Initialize a repository in a nested fixture path and compare repository discovery, work-tree state, bare state, and initial branch. A relative private template contains only the documented default metadata plus an empty hooks directory, avoiding installed sample hooks.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
mkdir -p nested/repo
cd nested/repo
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=../../fixture-template
git init -q -b topic .
git rev-parse --git-dir
git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree
git rev-parse --is-bare-repository
git symbolic-ref --short HEAD

cases.purpose: Compare repeated config values, case-insensitive key lookup, a command-line override, boolean conversion, and the resulting deterministic config file bytes.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
git init -q -b main .
git config user.name 'Config Fixture'
git config --add remote.origin.fetch '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*'
git config --add remote.origin.fetch '+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*'
git config --get-all remote.origin.fetch
git -c user.name=Override config --get USER.NAME
git config --get user.name
git config --bool core.bare
git config --get-regexp '^remote\.'

cases.purpose: Hash, read, type-check, and size-check a binary blob, then add/list/delete a lightweight tag ref. compare_tree is false because independently generated loose objects use zlib byte streams and reflogs include wall-clock timestamps; output includes the object ID, type, size, raw payload, and ref listing.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
git init -q -b main .
printf 'alpha\000beta\n' > payload.bin
object=$(git hash-object -w payload.bin)
printf 'object=%s\n' "$object"
git cat-file -t "$object"
git cat-file -s "$object"
printf 'payload-start:'
git cat-file blob "$object"
printf ':payload-end\n'
printf '%s\n' "$object" | git cat-file --batch-check
git update-ref refs/tags/blob-fixture "$object"
git show-ref --tags
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname) %(objecttype) %(objectname)' refs/tags
git update-ref -d refs/tags/blob-fixture
if git show-ref --tags; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'empty-tag-list-status=%d\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Stage paths including a space, inspect index entries and porcelain status, then compare a tracked edit and an untracked file with numstat. compare_tree is false because Git index entries store device, inode, and timestamp stat-cache values that differ between the independently created fixture trees.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
git init -q -b main .
printf 'one\n' > 'a file.txt'
printf 'two\n' > second.txt
git add -- 'a file.txt' second.txt
git ls-files --stage
git status --porcelain=v2 --untracked-files=all
printf 'edited\n' >> second.txt
printf 'new\n' > new.txt
git status --short --untracked-files=all
git diff --numstat
printf 'worktree bytes:\n'
while IFS= read -r row; do printf '%s\n' "$row"; done < 'a file.txt'
while IFS= read -r row; do printf '%s\n' "$row"; done < second.txt
while IFS= read -r row; do printf '%s\n' "$row"; done < new.txt

cases.purpose: Create two commits with fixed identities and dates, then compare full commit/tree/parent IDs, a commit-to-commit numstat, and clean branch status. compare_tree is false because index stat-cache fields, compressed object bytes, and reflog timestamps vary across isolated repositories; full object IDs in stdout verify the Git content independently.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
git init -q -b main .
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Parity Author' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='author@example.invalid'
export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Parity Committer' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='committer@example.invalid'
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='1750000000 +0000' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='1750000100 +0000'
printf 'first\n' > tracked.txt
git add tracked.txt
git commit -q -m first
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='1750000200 +0000' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='1750000300 +0000'
printf 'second\n' >> tracked.txt
git add tracked.txt
git commit -q -m second
git log --format='%H %T %P %an <%ae> %at %s' -2
git diff --numstat HEAD~1 HEAD
git status --short --branch

cases.purpose: Exercise fixture-local git mv and git rm on committed paths, then check staged status, index names, source/destination existence, and moved content. compare_tree is false because the committed index stat cache, compressed objects, and reflog timestamps are not byte-stable between isolated Git runs; file effects are also asserted in the script.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
git init -q -b main .
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Parity Author' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='author@example.invalid'
export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Parity Committer' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='committer@example.invalid'
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='1750000000 +0000' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='1750000100 +0000'
printf 'move me\n' > 'old name.txt'
printf 'remove me\n' > remove.txt
git add -- 'old name.txt' remove.txt
git commit -q -m base
git mv -- 'old name.txt' moved.txt
git rm -q -- remove.txt
git status --short --no-renames
git diff --cached --name-status --no-renames
git ls-files
test ! -e 'old name.txt'
test -f moved.txt
test ! -e remove.txt
IFS= read -r moved_content < moved.txt
printf 'moved-content=%s\n' "$moved_content"

cases.purpose: Preview and remove one untracked file inside the private fixture repository while retaining an ignored file; assertions check both resulting file states. compare_tree is false because the setup commit leaves an index stat cache, compressed objects, and timestamped reflog entries whose raw bytes differ across independent runs.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
git init -q -b main .
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Parity Author' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='author@example.invalid'
export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Parity Committer' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='committer@example.invalid'
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='1750000000 +0000' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='1750000100 +0000'
printf '*.log\n' > .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -q -m ignore-logs
printf 'fixture junk\n' > junk.txt
printf 'ignored fixture\n' > keep.log
git clean -n -- junk.txt
git clean -fq -- junk.txt
test ! -e junk.txt
test -f keep.log
printf 'junk-removed; ignored-retained\n'
git status --short --ignored
IFS= read -r row < keep.log
[[ $row == 'ignored fixture' ]]
printf '%s\n' "$row"

cases.purpose: Clone a committed relative-path repository locally, then verify the cloned commit, checked-out blob bytes, branch status, and source/clone path effects without using network transport. compare_tree is false because independent Git implementations may choose different local object-copy or hardlink strategies, and the repositories contain stat-cache and compressed-object bytes.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
mkdir source
(cd source; GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=../fixture-template git init -q -b main .)
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Clone Author' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='clone@example.invalid'
export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Clone Committer' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='clone-committer@example.invalid'
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='1750000000 +0000' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='1750000100 +0000'
printf 'clone payload\n' > source/file.txt
git -C source add file.txt
git -C source commit -q -m source-commit
git clone -q source copy
git -C copy log --format='%H %T %s' -1
git -C copy status --short --branch
printf 'cloned-content:'
git -C copy cat-file blob HEAD:file.txt
test -d copy/.git
test -f copy/file.txt
IFS= read -r row < copy/file.txt
[[ $row == 'clone payload' ]]
printf '%s\n' "$row"

cases.purpose: Check the fatal status for a missing object while preserving the command's diagnostic byte-for-byte with exact stderr; the script captures and prints the status so the fixture itself exits successfully. Init metadata and the remaining tree are compared in full.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
git init -q -b main .
if git cat-file -t 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'missing-object-status=%d\n' "$rc"
test "$rc" -eq 128

cases.purpose: Remote protocol behavior for clone, fetch, and push.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable in-namespace upload-pack/receive-pack mock with injected SSH or HTTP transport and deterministic protocol responses. The current fixture runner has no local peer injection; do not substitute a real network target.

cases.purpose: Signed commits and interactive editor-driven operations.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable PTY plus a fake signing helper and test-only key material created inside that fixture. This suite has no terminal or signing-service mock and must not read installed credentials.

cases.purpose: Distinguish unresolved names from a missing full object ID for -t, -s, -p, -e and an explicit object type; compare every status and exact diagnostic, with the initialized repository tree unchanged.
cases.script:
export GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p fixture-template/info fixture-template/hooks
printf "%s\n" "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." > fixture-template/description
printf '%s\n' "# git ls-files --others --exclude-from=.git/info/exclude" "# Lines that start with '#' are comments." > fixture-template/info/exclude
export GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR=fixture-template
git init -q -b main .
for flag in -t -s -p -e blob; do
 for name in 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 absent; do
  printf '%s %s\n' "$flag" "$name" >&2
  if git cat-file "$flag" "$name"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
  printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
 done
done
